EditTextPreference.title: Read-only API Key
EditTextPreference.dialogMessage: Create a System generated API key in Binance → Account → API Management. Enable only Enable Reading. Do not enable Spot & Margin Trading, Futures, Withdrawals, or Universal Transfer.

EditTextPreference.title: Read-only API Secret
EditTextPreference.dialogMessage: The secret is shown once. Keep it private and never enable trading or withdrawal permissions.

EditTextPreference.title: Account label
EditTextPreference.dialogMessage: Use Binance for the main account and Binance M for the second connection.

CheckBoxPreference.title: Sync Spot
CheckBoxPreference.dialogMessage: Includes both free assets and amounts locked in Spot orders.

CheckBoxPreference.title: Sync Funding
CheckBoxPreference.dialogMessage: Funding wallet used by Binance Pay, P2P and card-related flows.

CheckBoxPreference.title: Sync Earn
CheckBoxPreference.dialogMessage: Combines Flexible and Locked Simple Earn positions into the exchange-native Earn account.

CheckBoxPreference.title: Show separate exchange wallets
CheckBoxPreference.dialogMessage: On by default: matches Binance and ZenMoney account structure. Turn off only if you deliberately prefer one combined portfolio account.

CheckBoxPreference.title: Sync wallet transactions
CheckBoxPreference.dialogMessage: Imports completed external deposits and withdrawals, Binance Pay, P2P, Spot ↔ Funding and Simple Earn movements with stable Binance IDs. Trading fills and valuation noise are excluded.

EditTextPreference.title: Settlement assets to import
EditTextPreference.dialogMessage: Comma-separated USD-pegged assets. Balances always include every supported asset; this setting controls only historical deposits and withdrawals. Volatile coins need separate asset accounting and are intentionally excluded.

EditTextPreference.title: Load operations from
EditTextPreference.dialogMessage: External deposit and withdrawal history is loaded from this date. Binance exposes Pay, P2P, internal wallet and Earn history only for limited periods; later synchronizations continue incrementally.
